label: Gas stove or hob

questions.text: When was the gas hose last checked or changed?
questions.why: Old or cracked hoses can leak.
A yellow or uneven flame can mean blocked burners.

questions.text: Does the automatic ignition (if any) work first time?
questions.why: Repeated clicking can mean a fault.

questions.text: Is the kitchen well ventilated while cooking?
questions.why: Fresh air keeps gas from collecting.

questions.text: How often are the burners cleaned?
Have you ever smelled gas near the stove?
questions.why: A gas smell needs urgent attention.

care_tips.text: If you smell gas: close the gas supply, don't switch anything electrical on or off, open doors and windows to ventilate, and call your gas or service number from outside.
care_tips.why: A spark in a room full of gas can cause an explosion.

care_tips.text: Turn the knobs and the gas supply off when you finish cooking.
Have the gas hose checked, and replaced when it is old or cracked, by your gas provider or the brand's service.
Keep a window open or the chimney on while cooking.
Clean the burners as the manual describes once they are cool.
care_tips.why: Clean burners give a steady blue flame.

care_tips.text: If the flame stays yellow or uneven, contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: It can mean the gas is not burning properly.

care_tips.text: If the ignition keeps clicking without lighting, turn the knob off and contact the brand's service.

reminders.text: Check the gas hose for cracks and ask for it to be checked.
reminders.note: Check your manual and your gas provider's advice.
